$ xref profile report

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Usage
  2. Arguments and options
  3. Examples
  4. Hottest functions
  5. Hottest instructions
  6. Reading the output
  7. Provenance

Summarize a recorded profile (.xprof, from live profile or profile import): the hottest functions, basic blocks, source lines, caller paths or instructions, with self and total shares.

Usage

xref profile report [OPTIONS] <PROFILE>

Arguments and options

Arguments

<PROFILE>
The .xprof recording.

Options

--top <TOP>
Number of rows to print.
default 30
--by <BY>
What a row aggregates: function, basic block, source line, caller path or instruction [possible values: function, block, line, caller-path, instruction].
default function
--json
Print the report as JSON.
--folded <FOLDED>
Also write folded stacks (flame-graph input) to this file.
--within <WITHIN>
Keep samples whose call chain includes this function or address.
--window <WINDOW>
Select one captured trigger window (numbered from one).
--merge-windows
Report the union of all captured windows.

Examples

The profile is ripgrep filtering an endless input stream, recorded with live profile.

$ xref -b rg profile report rg.xprof --top 8

Reading the output

  • The first line: samples, lost and dropped samples, and partial=true when some call chains could not be unwound completely.
  • Each row: self share (samples in the function itself), total share (samples with the function anywhere on the stack), self sample count, and the frame: target:fn_ADDR for code in the binary, target:unknown for samples in the binary outside any known function, [kernel] or a library for the rest.
  • warning: lines name the reasons a chain stopped; they are counted, not hidden.

Provenance

Recorded with a development build of xref after 0.4.0 on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release). Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
